# site/assets/shots/seasalt.png
#
# A turn mid-decision, which is the only state that shows what the app is for:
# a hand of ten with the census on every card, the deck and both discard piles
# above it, the three tabs, a selected crab, and the hint box answering what
# that crab does at the moment it is touched. The CALL pill is live because the
# hand is worth seven.
#
# REPRODUCIBLE, unlike the older recipes here. The save is generated by
# tools_local/seasalt/seasalt_mkstate.cpp, which walks a real game with a fixed seed
# until it reaches a Play step with eight or more cards, five or more kinds and
# both piles live -- so replaying these taps gives the identical board every
# time. The whole contact sheet is built the same way:
#
#     ./tools_local/seasalt/seasalt_sheet.sh
#
# which writes qa-artifacts/seasalt_sheet.png and every screen in it, this shot
# among them (sheet_selected.png).

setup:
  c++ -std=c++17 -O2 -Isrc/apps_local/seasalt \
    src/apps_local/seasalt/SeaSaltCore.cpp tools_local/seasalt/seasalt_mkstate.cpp \
    -o /tmp/seasalt_mkstate
  /tmp/seasalt_mkstate call > fs_agent/.crosspoint/seasalt.sav

input:
  2000:TAP:120,635      # GAMES on the home shelf
  3600:TAP:240,605      # SEA SALT, last row of page one
  5600:TAP:240,535      # CONTINUE -- the saved board above
  7600:TAP:69,378       # the first hand card, a crab

shot:
  9200:./qa-artifacts/sheet_selected.bmp

# The card grid is hit-tested arithmetically from seasaltui::cardCellRect, the
# same function that draws it, so a tap at a cell centre cannot land anywhere
# else. Card cells are 106 wide with 7px gutters; the gap between two cards
# belongs to neither and a tap there is a deliberate miss.

downsample: PIL BOX, 960x1600 -> 480x800 8-bit grey
